skill.name: altllm-portal-auth
skill.description: Guides AltLLM Portal wallet authentication for the local altllm CLI, including external signing, session checks, and logout workflows.
skill.summary: Authenticate AltLLM Portal wallet sessions through the local altllm CLI.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: The skill supports a legitimate AltLLM Portal wallet-auth workflow, but it handles high-value wallet and session material. I confirmed risks around private-key input paths, unsafe argv private-key usage, hidden session-file persistence, and parent-directory shared-file references. No prompt-injection text or covert exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Wallet private-key input is documented as a normal login path.
remediation.suggestion: Make external challenge signing the primary flow and place private-key login behind explicit user confirmation and redaction guidance.

remediation.issue: Inline private keys are allowed through command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the inline private-key option from examples, or require a prominent warning before any argv-based private-key command.

remediation.issue: The skill references shared setup files through parent-directory paths.
remediation.suggestion: Package the shared guidance inside the skill directory or include reviewed text directly in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Portal session material is persisted in a hidden file under the user home directory.
remediation.suggestion: Document restrictive file permissions, token redaction, and safe cleanup behavior for the session file.

content.value_statement: Wallet login can expose private keys or create confusing local sessions. This skill guides safer AltLLM Portal authentication, external signing, status checks, and logout.
actual_capabilities: Guides wallet login for the local altllm CLI.
Prepares sign-in challenges for external wallet signing.
Verifies a nonce and signature to save a Portal session.
Checks saved Portal session status without exposing the token.
Logs out by removing the local Portal session file.
Explains EVM-only signature support and non-default host guidance.
limitations: It does not manage API keys, billing history, or payment links.
It requires a local altllm CLI build with wallet commands.
The backend currently supports EVM addresses and Ethereum-style signatures only.
Local logout removes the session file but does not revoke API keys.

use_cases.title: Connect a Developer Wallet
use_cases.description: Prepare and complete an AltLLM Portal wallet login without placing private keys in command arguments.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Local Session State
use_cases.description: Check the saved user, target origin, and forwarding status before running live CLI commands.

use_cases.title: Use External Signing
use_cases.description: Fetch a challenge for a wallet provider such as Privy, then verify the returned signature.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use altllm-portal-auth to check whether my saved Portal wallet session is valid before I run live commands.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Wallet Challenge
prompt_templates.prompt: Use altllm-portal-auth to prepare a login challenge for my wallet address. Stop after returning the challenge details for external signing.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Signed Challenge
prompt_templates.prompt: Use altllm-portal-auth to verify my signed challenge with the nonce and signature I provide, then confirm the saved session status.

prompt_templates.title: Review Host Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Use altllm-portal-auth to plan wallet login for a non-default AltLLM API host. Prefer external signing and identify private-key exposure risks.

output_examples.input: Prepare a wallet challenge for the default AltLLM Portal API.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns the challenge message, nonce, expiration, and signing instructions, then stops before any private-key use.

output_examples.input: Check my saved Portal login before deployment.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the saved user, session origin, target origin, and forwarding status without revealing the session token.

output_examples.input: Log out of my local Portal wallet session.
output_examples.output: The assistant removes the local session file and explains that API keys are not revoked by local logout.

best_practices: Prefer challenge preparation and external signing when a wallet provider is available.
Verify wallet address, chain, nonce, challenge host, and expiration before signing.
Check session status before live commands and protect the saved session file.
anti_patterns: Passing private keys directly in command arguments.
Auto-signing against non-default remote API hosts without reviewing the challenge.
Assuming local logout revokes server credentials or API keys.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with AltLLM Portal wallet login, challenge preparation, signature verification, session status, and local logout.

faq.question: Does it require my private key?
faq.answer: No. The preferred flow prepares a challenge so your wallet or provider can sign externally.

faq.question: Can it work with Privy?
faq.answer: Yes. Privy can be used when it returns a standard wallet signature for the challenge message.

faq.question: Where is the session stored?
faq.answer: The documented default path is a Portal CLI session file under the user home directory.

faq.question: Does status reveal the token?
faq.answer: No. The documented status command reports user and target details without printing the session token.

faq.question: Does logout revoke API keys?
faq.answer: No. Local logout removes the saved session file. It does not revoke API keys.
